articles.title: Kardashian curves: M&S launches £28 bodysuit with exaggerated hip padding
articles.summary: The ‘hip boost’ aims to create hourglass silhouette, much like Kim Kardashian’s shapewear brand’s padded shorts. For decades shapewear has been used to compress and cinch. But now there is a sub-genre emerging. Rather than shrinking a silhouette, it aims to add inches.
body: This week M&S launched a bodysuit that features exaggerated padding at the hip allowing the wearer to create an hourglass shape, or at least the illusion of one.
Similar to how bra inserts, AKA chicken fillets, are used to add extra volume to breasts, the £28 “hip boost” features pockets on each side of the suit that allow the wearer to add in enhancing pads.

Charlotte Davies, the director of lingerie at the retailer, says the idea stemmed from customer interest in “solutions that offer subtle enhancement alongside everyday comfort and confidence”, with the trend being driven by the catwalks and celebrities. The hip booster’s predecessors at M&S include padded bum shorts “to give the wearer a curvy, contoured look” and stick-on nipples for “a realistic raised profile beneath clothing”.

Kim Kardashian’s shapewear brand, Skims, launched shorts with hip padding last year. Many users online claim such type of strategic padding can help minimise “hip dips” – a phrase used to describe the natural inward curves between the hipbone and thigh bone.
points: The ‘hip boost’ aims to create hourglass silhouette, much like Kim Kardashian’s shapewear brand’s padded shorts.

articles.title: ‘This is colonialism for clicks’: the influencers attempting to meet and film the world’s most isolated tribes
articles.summary: A new breed of adventurer is chasing internet fame by targeting uncontacted peoples. Critics say they are risking the wellbeing of these remote communities – and their own lives. He set out from the beach around midnight, packing his camera, a coconut and a can of Diet Coke.
body: After hours of motoring across the Bay of Bengal, his destination came into view: a low-lying island, narrowly separating sea and sky. With the sun now high above him, Polyakov cut the engine and set his GoPro to record. “So, the goal,” he said, squinting towards the blinding-white beach. “Introduce this Palaeolithic tribe to modernity … Let’s land on this bitch.”

Polyakov was nearing North Sentinel Island, part of the Andaman archipelago governed by India. Venturing within 5km (3 miles) is strictly prohibited, let alone setting foot on shore, and authorities routinely patrol the surrounding waters. But Polyakov saw himself as on a mission: to see – and, more importantly, film – the Indigenous people who live there.
points: A new breed of adventurer is chasing internet fame by targeting uncontacted peoples.

articles.title: ‘It struck me as a minimalist tableau’: Henk Stam’s best phone picture
articles.summary: The Dutch photographer was pleased to capture this suitably orange scene in some toilets in Rotterdam. ‘I must admit I was very sceptical of phone photography at first,” Henk Stam says. Sixty years ago, he received his first camera for his 11th birthday.
body: This photo was taken in Portlantis, a visitors’ centre in the Port of Rotterdam that opened in spring 2025. Stam spent his working life in Canada but was born in the Netherlands and returned there on retirement. With a friend from his photo club, he went to visit Portlantis on a Monday, but found it closed. “As we were leaving, we noticed a large tour bus arriving filled with teenagers,” he says. “We simply joined the slipstream as they entered; no one batted an eyelid.”

There was still construction work being done inside, and as Stam nipped to the toilet, he spotted this worker’s legs sticking out of a cubicle, toolbox at his side. “It struck me as a minimalist tableau. Here, the royal family are referred to as the House of Orange, national teams and fans wear orange, and we festoon our streets with orange flags during major events. But I found it odd one would colour the toilets orange.”

Stam had left his camera with his friend, so grabbed this shot on his phone instead. He returned to Portlantis a few months later. “This time entering legitimately,” he says. “But nothing I captured then matched the uniqueness of this moment.”

articles.title: Sebastian Barry: ‘At 71, sex is somewhere between a memory and an ambition’
articles.summary: The author on dashed dreams of being the next Bob Dylan, cruel words from a revered poet and listening to his own snores. Born in Dublin, Sebastian Barry, 71, published his first novel in 1982.
body: When were you happiest? Purely and unconsciously, living on Greece’s Paros aged 25. Exhausted and happy, when our babies were small.
What is the trait you most deplore in yourself? Not listening, but I am training myself.
What do you most dislike about your appearance? The grotesqueries of old age.
If you could bring something extinct back to life, what would you choose? Selflessness in politicians.

articles.title: 18 Luxury Family Resorts in the US and Caribbean for Your Next Getaway
articles.summary: Whether you’re dreaming of the beach, the mountains, or Disney World, these resorts do it right.
body: There’s not enough room here to name all of the incredible luxury family resorts that one can find across the US and Caribbean. However, this list does represent the undeniable crowd-pleasers with every trick up their sleeve for both kids and parents—you know, those magical places that know how to anticipate every need and provide every imaginable comfort for a multigenerational group.

As a travel writer and a mom, I know that as families grow, so do their needs and tastes, which is why this list also aims to share the best luxury options for whatever stage of the game your crew is in right now. Families with toddlers and babies, for example, will love easy beach escapes at Cheval Blanc St-Barths and Winnetu Oceanside Resort in Martha’s Vineyard, while families planning a Walt Disney World vacation will see it through new eyes after a stay at the Four Seasons in Orlando. Older kids will be over the moon to take part in mountain adventures at Paws Up Montana, and mixed-age groups will be eyeing SoCal's Terranea for their next big gathering.

articles.title: Mariacarla Boscono on Wearing Chanel to Venice Film Festival: “I Feel Like Matthieu’s Princess”
articles.summary: Supermodel Mariacarla Boscono marked her fifth time on the lido wearing the newspaper print gown from the Chanel resort 2027 collection.
body: “This look is very special to me; Chanel is the fashion house closest to my heart. This year it’s even more special because it was designed by my dear friend Matthieu Blazy and his incredible team. The dress is simply a work of art, and I truly feel like a princess—Matthieu’s princess.”

With these words, Mariacarla Boscono shared her feelings shortly before—on the evening of Thursday, September 3—walking the red carpet at the 2026 Venice Film Festival for the premiere of Martin McDonagh’s *Wild Horse Nine *. The Italian supermodel attended this major film event wearing a dress from the Chanel Cruise 2026–2027 collection. Hers was a captivating return, combining the innate theatricality of her poise with a bold, sophisticated style steeped in historical references to haute couture.

The creation represents a perfect synthesis between the Parisian fashion house’s classic spirit and a vibrant avant-garde edge. Crafted from the finest, lightest tweed, the dress—chosen by stylist Ramona Tabita—features a sumptuous knotted structure that opens into a generous back neckline and culminates in a majestic train that skims the red carpet.
points: Supermodel Mariacarla Boscono marked her fifth time on the lido wearing the newspaper print gown from the Chanel resort 2027 collection.

articles.title: Street Style Rewind: What the Fashion Set Wore to the Shows in 2017
articles.summary: Ahead of the spring 2027 season, we’re throwing it back a decade to see what was all the rage in the streets.
body: Picture this: It’s 2017. Rodarte is showing on the runway; the short-form video platform du jour was Vine, and no one was more famous than Cameron Dallas, a catwalk and front-row habitué who hinted at the future of TikTok stars.

Today, Kylie Jenner might be all about that quiet luxury trend, but ten years ago she was making a splash at NYFW in a beaded denim short set from Simkhai. Of course, when we talk about 2017 catwalks, we can’t forget that today’s favorite sister duo, the Hadids, had just made a rare joint appearance at Fashion Week, walking out of Versace ’s supermodel-stuffed spring 2017 show. Take us back to the glory days!

As usual, there was just as much action off the runways as on. Milan attendees went hard on Alessandro Michele’s kooky and colorful Gucci while independent designers like Molly Goddard were also in heavy rotation. London was all about Christopher Kane, which only stirs up our excitement for his upcoming show for Mulberry. And it was the first and last time our street style photographer, Phil Oh, took vertical photos for his street style galleries—although when asked about it today, he can’t remember why and promises that it won’t ever be happening again.

articles.title: Pumpkin Chili
articles.summary: A can of pumpkin puree adds richness, body, and an autumnal hue to this speedy chili, letting the flavors of the spices, aromatics, and ground beef shine.
body: This pumpkin chili gets an entire can of pumpkin purée—but you’d hardly know it. Rather than making the chili taste like pumpkin, the purée gives it velvety richness, body, and an autumnal hue. (Be sure to buy pure pumpkin purée, not pumpkin pie filling.) Best of all, it comes together on the stovetop in just 35 minutes, making it an easy weeknight dinner that’s equally at home on game day or Halloween.

One unusual step makes this quick chili work: Instead of browning the ground beef separately, you’ll cook it directly in the spiced pumpkin mixture. This keeps the meat tender during the short cook time while a vigorous stir breaks it down into chunky, satisfying bits. Worcestershire sauce brings in plenty of savory depth. Top each bowl with sour cream, sliced jalapeño, and crunchy toasted pepitas.
Yes. Ground turkey and chicken both work well, but ground pork makes an especially rich, savory chili. Swap an equal amount of any of these for the beef and otherwise follow the recipe as written.
Yes. Canned butternut squash or even sweet potato works well here—just make sure it’s 100% purée, not pie mix or otherwise sweetened.

articles.title: Beauty Marks: The Best Beauty Looks of the Week
articles.summary: From Mary Beth Barone at Venice Film Festival to Doechii at Daisy Chain Fields Festival, these are the best beauty looks of the week.
body: Welcome back to Beauty Marks: Vogue ’s weekly edition of the best moments in celebrity beauty, from Vogue editors’ IG feeds, and all the glam of the fashion and pop culture landscapes. Each week, we curate the nail art to pin for your next nail appointment, new recruits to ‘Team Bob’, and major red carpet moments from the week’s most glamorous affairs. As always, it’s as much about celebrity beauty as it is about the makeup artists, hairstylists, and nail artists, as well as the creators crafting the trends you’re about to see everywhere.

This week, the best beauty looks played with volume and depth: victory rolls and dolly lashes, hair color with dimension and bold highlights swept across the visage. Glam became a costume: Eva Longoria played a Latina Peggy Bundy, while Alix Earle was a pastel blue-eyed pin-up.

Elsewhere, Hailey Bieber gave us a lesson in polished wedding guest glam, while Joey King played with the little details on the Practical Magic 2 promo tour. Venice Film Festival has also given us plenty of major beauty moments—and Mary Beth Barone really brought it for her first turn on the lido.
